$comment: Allowlist for check_fact_category_pinning.py (brief §5 C.7, SUDDHA-VACA Phase C lane:ci-lint). Every entry requires: file (repo-relative POSIX path, must match a Violation.file exactly), EITHER line (int, matched exactly against the violation's line number) OR pattern (a string matched as a regex, falling back to a plain substring match, against the violation's snippet text) — line is preferred when known since it is unambiguous; pattern is for cases where line drift is expected, and justification (a non-empty, specific, human-readable reason — 'pre-existing' alone is not sufficient, say WHY it's safe or why it's out of scope). An entry with neither line nor pattern never matches anything (fails closed, not open). Populated 2026-07-28 during the initial rollout scan against the live repo tree (this worktree, base main, before this wave's other lanes landed) — see the ci-lint lane's session report for the full disposition rationale of every entry. A matching entry covers one finding by default. max_occurrences freezes the observed count when several intentionally share a pattern.

entries.justification: NEW in PRATIJNA v4 Lane B1 (chart_reader_v4.py's special_points()). Intentionally returns ALL fact_key rows for a chart_facts fact_category (upapada_lagna / special_lagna / karaka_chara_position) — the caller needs every fact_key variant (e.g. upapada's 'sign' and 'lord_placement_verdict'), so there is nothing to reduce to a single row. fact_subject AND fact_key are both selected and preserved per output row, never collapsed into a dict keyed by subject alone — same safe shape as the pre-existing arudha_emitter.py/nakshatra_semantic_emitter.py entries below ('fact_key selected+preserved per row, no cross-fact_key collision hazard'). A deterministic ORDER BY fact_subject, fact_key, computed_at, fact_id is present on this query (visible in the surrounding source, not in this snippet) — this specific defect class (row silently picked at random among several sharing category+subject+key) is exactly what this function's own docstring documents and handles honestly for the live karaka_chara_position school-duplication case (both Jaimini karaka schools are returned, not one silently dropped).

entries.pattern: SELECT fact_id, fact_subject FROM chart_facts WHERE chart_id = %s AND ayanamsha_id = %s AND fact_category = 'sensitive_degree_check'
entries.justification: AUDITED set-valued whole-category read (2026-09-29, l3/gochara-autonomous-wp0-7), bo_upaya.py precedent. The result builds a fact_id -> fact_subject map over EVERY 'sensitive_degree_check' row (facts.sensitive_checks, line 269-271) used later only as a membership/lookup table (line 346). No row is selected or reduced by fact_category alone; there is no single-row misselection surface. Pinning one fact_key would BREAK the semantics (the map needs all keys of the category).

entries.pattern: SELECT fact_subject, fact_key, fact_value_text, fact_value_num FROM chart_facts WHERE chart_id = %s AND fact_category = 'ashtakavarga_kakshya_boundary'
entries.justification: AUDITED set-valued multi-key assembler (2026-09-29, l3/gochara-autonomous-wp0-7), get_kp_cusps.ts:140 precedent. _fetch_kakshya_boundaries reads EVERY fact_key of the category and assembles a per-subject dict keyed BY fact_key (start_deg/end_deg/lord per kakshya); the engine consumes the assembled boundary set, never a category-only row. A single fact_key pin would drop the sibling keys the assembler requires. Empty-set fallback is honest (WP5 H-1a flag).

AUDITED set-valued IDENTITY digest (2026-10-02, Pravāha B6 R9-8/da0b): SQL_AV_DONOR_IDENTITY reads EVERY fact_key of the category 'ashtakavarga_bindu_contributor' for the chart, per ayanāṁśa, and returns only a row COUNT and a sha256 over the canonical ordered (fact_subject | fact_key | fact_value_num) tuples — fact_key is part of the digested content. It never selects one fact by category; it is the frozen Stage-1 input `av_donor_rows` (presence + content identity of the donor-row set, reconciled live before any window row is read). A single fact_key pin would make the identity blind to the sibling keys it exists to detect. Read-only; touches no window row.
